review_notes:
I read all 242 lines of ContactGeometry.lean. I also read the upstream definitions in Axis.lean (axisDirection, axisHeight, axisHeight_zero, axisHeight_add) and checked how this file's declarations are used in ShiftedBlocks, ReversedContacts, LateContacts, Main, ContactBins and ExperimentContact. A grep found no `@[simp]` attribute anywhere in the DirectionalWalk directory. As a result, every Bool-indexed definition here (placedAxis, placedWidth, opposedAnchor) has to be unfolded by hand with `Bool.false_eq_true`/`↓reduceIte` each time it is used. The additive lemmas about axisHeight (neg, sum, opposite, step_self) are also passed to simp by name every time. That repeated boilerplate is the basis for all three findings.

I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemmas compile or that existing `simp only` calls still close afterwards. The `rfl` proofs should work because the definitions are plain `if b then … else …` on a Bool literal, but this is untested. The proposed simp set rewrites in one direction only: it pushes axisHeight inward and removes oppositeStep/placedAxis. None of the proposed lemmas rewrites back, so I see no cycle risk. The one interaction to watch is between a simp `axisHeight_opposite` and the bare `placedAxis` unfolding. Once `placedAxis_true` fires first, the two compose cleanly. The later wrappers axisHeight_step_opposite (ContactBins) and the ExperimentContact total lemmas depend on this file, so I did not treat them as independent replacements. The measure-theoretic lemmas (lines 160–240) use no custom simp interface beyond `Set.mem_Icc` etc., and I found nothing to report there.

findings.excerpt: def placedAxis {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (b : Bool) : Step d := if b then oppositeStep e else e
findings.problem: `placedAxis e b` is only ever used at the literals `false` and `true`, but there are no evaluation lemmas for those cases. Every use has to unfold the definition and then reduce the `if` by hand. In this file that happens four times (lines 108, 110, 112, 113: `simp only [placedAxis,Bool.false_eq_true,↓reduceIte]`, and `simp only [placedWidth,placedAxis,↓reduceIte] at *`). The same thing happens downstream in Main.lean:137 and LateContacts.lean:190. In Main.lean:139 a manual `change` is needed to turn `placedAxis (i,true) true` into `oppositeStep (i,true)`. Unfolding at `at *` also exposes `if` terms in every hypothesis, which is the kind of unwanted expansion a canonical simp lemma would prevent.
findings.proposed_change:
Add canonical Bool-case simp lemmas right after the definitions:
```lean
@[simp] lemma placedAxis_false {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) : placedAxis e false = e := rfl
@[simp] lemma placedAxis_true {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) : placedAxis e true = oppositeStep e := rfl
@[simp] lemma placedWidth_false {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) :
    placedWidth e false = slabRecords (axisDirection e) := rfl
@[simp] lemma placedWidth_true {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) :
    placedWidth e true = slabRecords (axisDirection (oppositeStep e)) := rfl
```
Then replace `simp only [placedAxis,Bool.false_eq_true,↓reduceIte]` with `simp only [placedAxis_false]` (or plain `simp`), and drop the `change` in Main.lean.
findings.benefit: The normal form `placedAxis e true ↦ oppositeStep e` and `placedAxis e false ↦ e` is reached directly. The definition never has to be unfolded, so no `if` appears in other hypotheses. Downstream proofs stop repeating the `Bool.false_eq_true`/`↓reduceIte` sequence. Together with axisDirection_opposite / axisHeight_opposite, simp can then reduce `axisDirection (placedAxis e true)` all the way to `-axisDirection e`.

findings.excerpt: if b then -stepVector e + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range i, wordEnd (Z (true,j))
findings.problem: `opposedAnchor` is also an `if` on a Bool that is always a literal at use sites, and it has no case lemmas. Every consumer writes `simp only [opposedSite,opposedAnchor,Bool.false_eq_true,↓reduceIte]` or a variant. This happens here at lines 92, 149 and 153, and downstream in ShiftedBlocks.lean:164 and ReversedContacts.lean:18, 111 and 122. The same unfolding pattern repeated in seven places means the definition has no usable simp interface.
findings.proposed_change:
Add
```lean
@[simp] lemma opposedAnchor_false {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (Z : TwoTape (Word d)) (i : ℕ) :
    opposedAnchor e Z false i = -(∑ j ∈ Finset.range (i+1), wordEnd (Z (false,j))) := rfl
@[simp] lemma opposedAnchor_true {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (Z : TwoTape (Word d)) (i : ℕ) :
    opposedAnchor e Z true i = -stepVector e + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range i, wordEnd (Z (true,j)) := rfl
```
and have the call sites use `simp only [opposedSite, opposedAnchor_false]` / `opposedAnchor_true` instead of unfolding plus `↓reduceIte`. `opposedSite` can stay unfolded explicitly. It is a non-recursive sum, and leaving it out of the default simp set avoids unwanted expansion.
findings.benefit: Each Bool case gets a stated, stable normal form. Call sites become shorter and no longer depend on how the `if` is elaborated (`Bool.false_eq_true` is only there because `if false = true` needs that rewrite). The meaning of each branch is also documented at the definition.

findings.excerpt:
lemma axisHeight_neg {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (x : Site d) :
    axisHeight e (-x) = -axisHeight e x := by
findings.problem: `axisHeight e` is an additive map `Site d → ℤ`. This file proves the structural rules for it (neg, sum, opposite step, value on its own step vector), and Axis.lean proves zero and add. None of them is tagged `@[simp]` and the map is not bundled as an `AddMonoidHom`. So whenever an `axisHeight` of a compound site has to be computed, the whole rule set is listed by hand. Line 92 passes `axisHeight_neg,axisHeight_add,axisHeight_sum,axisHeight_step_self`, and line 35 passes `axisHeight_add`. Downstream, ExperimentContact.lean:343 passes `axisHeight_add,…,axisHeight_opposite` and AxisBridges.lean:49 passes `axisHeight_add`. Each rule pushes `axisHeight` inward through `+`, `-`, `∑` or `oppositeStep`, or evaluates a closed term. None rewrites back toward a compound argument, so the set terminates and has no competing orientation.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `axisHeight_opposite`, `axisHeight_neg`, `axisHeight_sum` and `axisHeight_step_self` with `@[simp]`, together with the upstream `axisHeight_zero` and `axisHeight_add` in Axis.lean (and `axisDirection_opposite` for the analogous direction rule). A stronger option is to provide `def axisHeightHom (e : Step d) : Site d →+ ℤ` with a `@[simp]` coe lemma, so that Mathlib's `map_add`, `map_neg`, `map_sum` and `map_zero` simp lemmas apply automatically and the hand-written `axisHeight_sum` induction is no longer needed.
findings.benefit: `simp [opposedAnchor_true, hp, hm, tapeHeight]` would then compute `-axisHeight e (opposedAnchor e Z b i)` without the caller remembering which homomorphism rules to include. Combined with the placedAxis lemmas, `axisHeight (placedAxis e true) x` would also reduce automatically to `-axisHeight e x`. That removes the `rw [axisHeight_opposite] at hh` steps here and in ContactBins.axisHeight_step_opposite.
